referees.quote: This report is very novel and timely, thus I recommend the manuscript for publication in Nature Communications after a revision considering the following points

it remains unclear whether the work constitutes a significant advance to justify publication in Nature Communications... the manuscript does not convincingly demonstrate that mechanical readout and writing provide a clear conceptual or practical advantage

we advise against publication in the present form until this major item is properly addressed. To substantiate force-based writing, the authors must demonstrate reversible state control using a nonmagnetic tip

note: Recommendations are taken from Version 0, the first round in this file. There is no sign of a transfer from another journal. R1 labels some points 'MAJOR', but every request is for clarification, discussion or citations, with no new data, so it is rated minor revision. R2 is a borderline call: the report doubts the significance for this journal, which fits 'reject', but it is hedged ('remains unclear') and lists clarifications, so 'major revision' is a defensible alternative. R3 writes as 'we', which may mean co-reviewers, but no separate co-signing referee is identified, so it is listed once. R3 demands new experiments (nonmagnetic tip, tip-field modeling, field- and hyperfine-resolved statistics), hence major revision rather than reject.
